clauses.text:
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Civil Service Act (22 Stat. 403) 
and section 1753 of the Revised Statutes, 
and as President of the United States, I 
hereby amend Executive Order No. 9949, 
entitled “Modifying Executive Order' No. 
9721, Providing for the Transfer of 
Personnel to Certain Public Interna­
tional Organizations” , by striking out the 
words “within five years from the date 
of his transfer to such Board” , occurring 
in the second paragraph of the said or­
der, and inserting in lieu thereof the 
words “on or before December 31, 1953”.

EO 10415 is a one-sentence strike-and-insert amendment of the one-person order EO 9949. By the strike-and-insert ruling the amended clause continues until the parent order ends; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (which also lists EO 9949 and EO 9721). operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 845-1416 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10415.txt, 17 FR 10899): signed 1952-12-02; amends Executive Order 9949 (a one-person order of April 17, 1948 modifying paragraph 3(a) of Executive Order 9721 for a named Federal Communications Commission employee transferring to the International Frequency Registration Board) by striking the words that limit his reemployment rights to service terminated within five years from the date of his transfer and inserting a limit of on or before December 31, 1953. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments (option B), the amendment is a clause that continues, as amended, until the parent order ends; the parent EO 9949 is itself named in the EO 12553 table (offset 5212 of the held EO 12553 text), as is EO 9721 (offset 1105). The December 31, 1953 date limits the time within which the employee's service had to end to qualify; it is a condition deadline written into the clause, not an end of the order, and is treated as functionally spent on 1953-12-31 by analogy to the report-deadline ruling (owner ruling 2026-10-21, option C). Alternative reading, disclosed for the reviewer: the clause could be read to lapse by its own terms after 1953-12-31 because the modified condition could no longer be met by a later termination; the held evidence does not show whether the employee's service ended before that date or whether any reemployment right accrued, so no earlier end is established. Earlier candidate end under the unnamed-instruments ruling (owner ruling 2026-10-21, option C): Executive Order 10804, signed 1959-02-12 (held text jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_10804.txt, section 2 at offsets 1193-2145), revoked Executive Order 9721 and Executive Order 10103 except for employees then serving with an international organization and for rights vested before the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act; it does not name EO 9949 or EO 10415, so it is not treated as their end. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10415 appears in the table's column of order numbers at offset 10390 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt (the held OCR prints the numbers and the subjects in separate blocks, so identification rests on the number). EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, February 25, 1986; the filing date (2-26-86) and the printing date are not effective dates. The dossier flag target provision not located: EO:9721 concerns EO 9721's own text, which is cited by the parent chain only; it does not name EO 10415.
